entry.title: Zig: The Honest Systems Language You Have Been Ignoring
entry.summary: A practical introduction for developers who want control without chaos If you have been writing C for years and quietly resenting it, or if you tried Rust and got intimidated by the borrow checker on day two, Zig might be the language you have been waiting for. Zig is a general-purpose systems programming language created by Andrew Kelley in 2016. It is free, open-source (MIT licensed), and designed with one clear ambition: be a better C. Not a replacement for Rust, not a competitor to Go -- a sharper, more honest version of C. The official tagline from the Zig team sums it up well: Zig is built for "robustness, optimality and maintainability." It does not introduce new paradigms. It does not hide things from you. It just removes the parts of C that have been quietly ruining your week for …
